data.description:
Scope: `src/rebar/_store/**`, `reducer/**`, `graph/**`, `_snapshot/**`. ~230 lines leave, mostly relocations.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE RESULT — this shard establishes that comment triage CANNOT fix the two size-pressured files here, and the epic must not pretend otherwise. `_store/event_append.py` (791/800) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777/800) recovers ~3. Their comments ARE the replay-compat justifications. The real seams were identified instead: the two `_recover_from_*` helpers in event_append (`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`; ~140 lines) and `process_snapshot`'s four migration blocks in _processors (~80 lines). Those splits are OUT OF SCOPE here.

Verified stale: `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present in `KEY_MAP` directly below it AND cites a module path that does not exist; `_store/gitutil.py:3-4` claims it 'imports nothing from rebar.*' while :214 imports from `rebar._commands.fsck`; `_store/hlc.py:35-36` says a kill-switch reverts 'for one release' — four schema bumps ago — over a still-wired, still-tested code path; `reducer/_filters.py:1-11` justifies itself by a bash/Python duality that no longer exists.

`reducer/_version.py:39-66` duplicates the wire-format changelog that `docs/event-schema.md` also holds in a PARTIAL, STALE copy (has v2/v3, missing v4/v5). Two homes, one drifting.

Cheapest win in the whole audit: `graph/_graph.py:250-254` states the same sentence twice, once as a noqa suffix and once as the block below it.

The do_not_move list here is the most important of the six: 21 entries, with `reducer/_processors.py:719-774` flagged as highest-risk — four SNAPSHOT-restore migration guards where relocating the rationale makes live guards look like dead defensive code, one of which explicitly warns the guard must NOT run unconditionally because the else-branch would clobber a recorded channel with 'unknown'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost
## CORRECTION (plan-review preempt, parent 373f disposition vocabulary)

Superseding ACs below encode the 373f disposition rules, the verified-stale corrections (each
confirmed against the code), the two-homes changelog consolidation (info must be ADDED to the
canonical home before the duplicate is collapsed), and the highest-risk do_not_move set (the
snapshot-restore migration guards). This shard's NEGATIVE RESULT stands: the two size-pressured
files are NOT fixed by comment triage.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one parent-373f
      label: RELOCATE (to docs, reduced to a one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE, or
      CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a comment documenting CURRENT runtime behavior / a live
      invariant is CORRECTED in place; DELETE only when its referent no longer exists. Every
      DELETE records its reason (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) in the commit body.
- [x] These verified-stale comments are CORRECTED in place (referent still LIVE):
      `_store/gitutil.py:3-4` ("imports nothing from rebar.*" is false — line ~214 has a
      FUNCTION-LOCAL `from rebar._commands.fsck import _resolve_tracker_git_dir`; correct to
      "no MODULE-LEVEL rebar imports; one deferred in-function import"); `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28`
      (the docstring's Key-mapping block must enumerate the FOUR live maps — KEY_MAP,
      COMMENT_KEY_MAP, DEP_KEY_MAP, INBOUND_KEY_MAP — and its FIRST line cites the STALE package
      path `ticket_reducer/llm_format.py`; the module now lives at `reducer/llm_format.py` (the
      package was renamed `ticket_reducer`->`reducer`). CORRECT that header path to
      `reducer/llm_format.py` (or drop the bare-path line) and make the enumeration match the four
      live maps' key sets); `_store/hlc.py:35-36` ("reverts ... for one release"
      is stale by four schema bumps over a still-wired, still-tested REBAR_HLC=0 path; correct the
      "one release" phrasing, KEEP the kill-switch description).
- [x] `reducer/_filters.py:1-11` justifies itself by a bash/Python duality that no longer exists:
      RELOCATE any still-true content and DELETE the obsolete duality justification (reason:
      referenced-artifact-gone — the bash side is gone).
- [x] Two-homes changelog consolidation (NO information loss): `reducer/_version.py:39-66` and
      `docs/event-schema.md` both hold the wire-format changelog; docs is PARTIAL/STALE (has
      v2/v3, missing v4/v5). FIRST bring `docs/event-schema.md` to the COMPLETE set (add the v4
      and v5 entries from `_version.py`), THEN collapse the `_version.py` prose changelog to a
      one-line "see docs/event-schema.md" citation. The canonical home must be complete before
      the code copy is reduced. Observable oracle:
      `grep -q 'v4' docs/event-schema.md && grep -q 'v5' docs/event-schema.md` passes AND the
      `_version.py` changelog comment block (~39-66) collapses to a single citation line
      (`grep -c '^# v[2-5]' src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` returns 0 afterward).
- [x] `graph/_graph.py:250-254` states the same sentence twice (a `# noqa: BLE001` suffix AND the
      block comment below it): KEEP the `# noqa` pragma line intact (DO_NOT_MOVE), DELETE the
      redundant block comment that restates it (reason: superseded — duplicate of the pragma
      rationale).
- [x] NEGATIVE RESULT preserved: `_store/event_append.py` (791/800) and `reducer/_processors.py`
      (777/800) are NOT size-fixed by comment triage — their comments are replay-compat
      justifications. Recover only the trivially-recoverable lines (~10 / ~3); DO NOT strip
      load-bearing replay-compat rationale to chase headroom. The real splits (the four
      `_recover_from_*` helpers — `_recover_from_unmerged` and `_recover_from_invalid_object`; and `process_snapshot`'s SNAPSHOT-restore migration guards) are OUT OF SCOPE.
- [x] HIGHEST-RISK do_not_move (verbatim): `reducer/_processors.py:719-774` — the four
      SNAPSHOT-restore migration guards. Relocating their rationale would make live guards look
      like dead defensive code; one guard's comment explicitly warns it must NOT run
      unconditionally (the else-branch would clobber a recorded channel with 'unknown'). These
      stay verbatim.
- [x] A `## da4c` section is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, and it
      records EACH comment unit dispositioned DO_NOT_MOVE/KEEP as one `path:line — reason` row
      (the count is whatever the triage yields — an OUTPUT, not a target). Observable oracle: the
      section MUST contain, at minimum, a row for `reducer/_processors.py:719-774` (the four
      snapshot-restore guards) — verify with
      `grep -A40 '## da4c' .joe-janitor/tools.md | grep -q '_processors.py:719-774'`. Lint/type
      pragmas and test-introspected docstrings encountered in scope are recorded as DO_NOT_MOVE.
- [x] The actual recovered comment-line count is measured (by diff) and recorded on this ticket
      as an OUTPUT, not a target.
- [x] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass unchanged.
